title: Water-modulated conformational heterogeneity underlies multiple timescales of primary charge separation in photosystem II
task: Resolve multi-exponential kinetics of primary charge separation in Photosystem II
key_results: Water-modulated conformational heterogeneity explains multi-exponential charge separation kinetics with calculated lifetimes (<250 fs, 386 fs, 2.7 ps) matching experimental observations; single dominant intermediate radical pair (Chl_D1^+Pheo_D1^-) identified
comments: The attribution of complex kinetics to solvent-protein dynamics rather than parallel pathways is elegant, though the interplay between structural fluctuations and quantum tunneling rates warrants deeper exploration.

model_io.model: Atomistic molecular dynamics + quantum dynamics simulations of PSII reaction center

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-exponential charge separation arises from parallel pathways with chemically distinct radical pairs
hypotheses.result: Rejected; water-modulated conformational heterogeneity of single pathway explains kinetics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic water channels near oxygen-evolving complex modulate protein-solvent structural fluctuations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; water dynamics govern multi-exponential kinetics alongside pre-equilibration in excited-state manifold

title: Structural basis of nonmuscle myosin-2 autoinhibition mechanisms
task: Elucidate autoinhibitory mechanism of nonmuscle myosin-2 in 10S conformation
key_results: 53-nm cryo-EM structure of full-length NM2B reveals tri-segmented tail fold sequestering actin-binding and filament assembly interfaces; four distinct 10S conformations reveal conformational landscape
comments: High-resolution structural insights into a functionally critical autoinhibited state should enable rational therapeutic targeting of cytoskeletal diseases, though functional validation of the proposed sequestration mechanism would strengthen mechanistic claims.

model_io.model: Cryo-EM of full-length human NM2B

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tri-segmented tail fold sequesters actin-binding and filament assembly interfaces in autoinhibited state
hypotheses.result: Structural analysis confirms asymmetric heavy/light chain arrangement supports this sequestration model

title: SPOP-mediated nuclear ubiquitination degradation of p62/SQSTM1 contributes to HR repair
task: Elucidate SPOP-mediated p62/SQSTM1 nuclear ubiquitination in homologous recombination repair
key_results: SPOP-p62 nuclear interaction enhanced upon DNA damage; nuclear ubiquitination of p62 at K7 by SPOP leads to degradation, upregulating RAD51 and FLNA and enhancing HR efficiency; p62 SBC motif mutations (S276Y/S277G/S277I) increase radiotherapy sensitivity by impairing HR
comments: Nuclear ubiquitination-mediated protein degradation via SPOP-p62 fine-tunes HR efficiency—patient mutations disrupting this axis offer biomarkers for radiotherapy sensitivity.

model_io.model: Cancer cells with DNA damage and SPOP-p62 interaction

hypotheses.hypothesis: SPOP-mediated nuclear p62 ubiquitination and degradation upregulates RAD51/FLNA and enhances HR
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; p62 SBC mutations prevent degradation, impair HR, and increase radiotherapy sensitivity

title: A cholesterol-dependent LRRC8A-caveolin-1 axis sustains KRAS/EGFR signaling, ribosome biogenesis and growth in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
task: Establish LRRC8A-caveolin-1 axis in PDAC proliferation and biosynthesis
key_results: LRRC8A drives proliferation-associated volumetric S-phase expansion; forms cholesterol-dependent complex with CAV1; LRRC8A or CAV1 disruption reduces KRAS/EGFR signaling, ribosome biogenesis, and protein synthesis; LRRC8A inhibition suppresses PDO growth
comments: Volume-regulated anion channels coordinate lipid raft dynamics and oncogenic signaling—targeting LRRC8A-CAV1 exploits a collateral dependency linking osmotic adaptation to metabolic expansion.

model_io.model: PDAC cells and patient-derived organoids with LRRC8A/CAV1 inhibition or cholesterol depletion

hypotheses.hypothesis: LRRC8A-CAV1 complex sustains PDAC growth via cholesterol-dependent coordination of membrane dynamics and oncogenic signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; disruption of LRRC8A-CAV1 or cholesterol depletion impairs biosynthesis and suppresses PDO growth

title: Fas acts as a T cell co-stimulatory receptor via both death domain-independent and -dependent mechanisms
task: Characterize Fas death domain-independent and -dependent co-stimulatory mechanisms in T cells
key_results: Fas localizes at immune synapse and lowers TCR activation threshold via DD-independent mechanism; DD-dependent FADD-caspase-8-RIPK1-TAK1 cascade activates gene expression; caspase-8 inhibition prevents death while promoting RIPK1-dependent co-stimulation
comments: Fas integrates multiple spatial and signaling modes to synergize with TCR—caspase-8 serves as a bifurcation point between death and co-stimulation, offering a molecular lever for enhancing T cell responses.

model_io.model: T cell stimulation with FasL and TCR engagement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fas acts as co-stimulatory receptor via both DD-independent threshold lowering and DD-dependent RIPK1-TAK1 signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dual mechanisms identified; caspase-8 inhibition favors co-stimulation over death

title: ATF4 coordinates amino acid and nucleotide synthesis with selective protein translation to ensure proper DNA replication timing in leukemia cells
task: Determine ATF4 role in coordinating amino acid, nucleotide metabolism, and protein synthesis for DNA replication timing in leukemia
key_results: ATF4 promotes amino acid biosynthesis enzymes and tRNA charging enzyme transcription; ATF4 inhibition limits nucleotide biosynthesis and replication machinery, disrupts replication timing, and induces leukemia cell differentiation and death
comments: ATF4 coordinates metabolic and translational programs to maintain DNA replication fidelity—an integrated view of how cancer cells sustain replication acceleration through selective protein synthesis.

model_io.model: Acute leukemia cells with ATF4 inhibition

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATF4 coordinates amino acid and nucleotide metabolism with selective protein translation to maintain replication timing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ATF4 inhibition disrupts all three processes and leads to replication timing errors and cell death

title: Soluble CD95L triggers Caspase-10-driven reactive oxygen species production in neutrophils and aggravates anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-vasculitis
task: Elucidate CD95L-driven ROS production mechanism in ANCA-associated vasculitis neutrophils
key_results: sCD95L triggers caspase-10-mediated cleavage of OTULIN deubiquitinase at D31/D54, unleashing LUBAC E3 ligase activity and mitochondrial ROS; blocking CD95 signaling reduces ROS and alleviates vasculitis in mouse models
comments: Non-apoptotic death receptor signaling converges on ROS via deubiquitinase substrate cleavage—a potentially targetable mechanism in autoimmune disease.

model_io.model: AAV neutrophil exposure to sCD95L
Mouse AAV and crescentic glomerulonephritis models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Caspase-10 drives ROS production by cleaving OTULIN and activating LUBAC in AAV neutrophils
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; proteomic and functional data support caspase-10→OTULIN cleavage→LUBAC activation cascade

title: A modular chromosomal passenger complex rewires chromosome segregation in Plasmodium berghei

key_results: ARK1 depletion causes multipolar spindles, kinetochore misalignment, and failed chromosome partitioning; modular CPC composition varies between male gametogenesis (minimal ARK1-INCENP-A) and meiosis (ARK1 plus INCENP-B and checkpoint proteins)
comments: Stage-specific CPC rewiring in a parasite reveals developmental plasticity in segregation control with potential transmission-blocking applications.

model_io.model: P. berghei male gametogenesis and meiosis

hypotheses.hypothesis: ARK1 forms a minimal CPC during male gametogenesis but recruits additional components during meiosis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; stage-specific modularity supports efficient gamete formation and safe chromosome inheritance

title: Divergent 3D genome architecture of male germ cells across vertebrates

comments: High-resolution Hi-C of germ cells across 350 million years of divergence reveals structure-function co-evolution but MSCI escape in marsupials suggests incomplete regulatory conservation.

model_io.model: Comparative germ line Hi-C and RNA-seq across eutherian, marsupial, reptile lineages

hypotheses.hypothesis: 3D genome architecture in germ cells is shaped by chromosome morphology and genome size across lineages
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; lineage-specific folding constrains loop formation and interactions during meiosis

title: Single-molecule imaging reveals RNA polymerase II dynamics and TAF1-dependent promoter-proximal pause release

key_results: ~94% of Pol II chromatin-associated events dissociate within tens of seconds; TAF1 degradation reduces Pol II clustering and increases global pausing index; substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity in productive elongation fraction
comments: Single-molecule tracking reveals that productive elongation is rate-limiting and TAF1 promotes pause release, but most Pol II events terminate rapidly—highlighting the bottleneck nature of early transcription.

model_io.model: Single-molecule imaging of Pol II in live human cells
TAF1 acute degradation

hypotheses.hypothesis: TAF1 promotes Pol II pause release and entry into productive elongation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; TAF1 degradation increases pausing index and reduces clustering of long-lived binding events

comments: First report of a food-origin peptide antagonist of IL-2Rβ with pleiotropic anti-pyroptotic and tissue-regenerative effects, though the molecular basis of microbiome restoration remains unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RDP3 functions as IL-2Rβ peptide antagonist to suppress PI3K and block NLRP3/GSDMD pyroptosis

title: NLRP3 inflammasome characterization in first-trimester, preterm, and term human villous placenta

key_results: First-trimester placentas show highest cytokine concentrations and NLRP3 protein despite low transcripts; preterm and term placentas exhibit 'primed but restrained' phenotype with pro-caspase-1 and gasdermin D accumulation but minimal caspase-1 activation
comments: Distinct inflammasome profiles across gestation suggest developmental stage-specific regulation of immunity at the maternal-fetal interface, with preterm placenta showing inflammasome priming without proportional activation.

model_io.model: Human villous placental tissue from first-trimester, preterm, and term pregnancies

hypotheses.hypothesis: NLRP3 inflammasome exhibits distinct profiles across pregnancy stages
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; first-trimester shows high activation, while preterm/term show primed but restrained phenotype without proportional downstream caspase-1 activation

comments: HMGB3 orchestrates glycolysis-driven histone lactylation and Wnt signaling to activate c-myc—a multi-level oncogenic circuit potentially vulnerable to dual inhibition.

hypotheses.hypothesis: HMGB3 promotes EC progression via histone lactylation and Wnt/β-catenin-mediated c-myc activation

comments: Novel integration of metagenomics, cytokines, and viral serology reveals age-sex-specific immune-virus dynamics; mechanistic drivers of biphasic patterns remain unclear.
